In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which vitamin C is transported into human neutrophils and the regulation of this process by the colony-stimulating growth factors.
the role of vitamin C in neutrophil function and the mechanisms regulating its uptake in human host defense.
the mechanisms by which the CSFs regulate the uptake and intracellular accumulation of vitamin C in host defense cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CSFs stimulate increased transport of ascorbic and dehydroascorbate in human myeloid cells by enhancing the oxidation of aspartate to dehydroascorbat and increasing the affinity of the facilitative glucose transporter for dehydroascorbat.

the CSFs increase the transport of vitamin C into human neutrophils and HL-60 cells by increasing the oxidation and conversion of vitamin C into its transportable moiety, dehydroascorbate, as well as by increasing the transport of this moiety through the facilitative hexose transporters.
the CSFs increase the uptake of vitamin C by human neutrophils and HL-60 cells through the facilitative sugar transporter GLUT 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSFs stimulate increased transport of vitamin D in neutrophils and that increased vitamin D uptake in neutrophilic cells is a mechanism for CSFs to enhance the host defense functions of these cells.
vitamin C uptake by myeloid cells is regulated by the CSFs through increased oxidation of ascorbate and increased transport of the oxidized form dehydroascorbate.
the CSFs stimulate increased transport of vitamin D in human host defense cell through the facilitative transporters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin C transport is increased in neutrophils and other myeloid cells in response to the CSFs.
the CSFs increase the transport and accumulation of vitamin C in neutrophils and other myeloid host defense cells.
vitamin C transport in myeloid cells is regulated by the CSFs, which are central modulator of the production, differentiation, and function of these cells.
